name: Ohio & Cleveland (AI-written, not yet reviewed)
description: 55 questions on Ohio and Cleveland: landmarks, teams' history, food and famous Ohioans, from easy to hard (18 easy, 19 medium, 18 hard), written by Claude. Every question and answer needs checking by a person before anybody plays it.

source.name: Written by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) on 2026-10-05, from its own knowledge plus the pages each item cites: no API call. Each item's `source` names the page its fact was confirmed on, or "common knowledge" with a reason where the fact is universal. Then fact-checked item by item by a second Claude pass on 2026-10-05 (every cited page re-fetched and read for the fact; `checked` keeps who checked it and what was fixed; items that could not be made right, and near-duplicates of other packs, were deleted). A person still reviews it by playing. On 2026-10-07 every item whose `source` said "common knowledge" was given a real source instead: a page fetched that day that states the fact, with the supporting phrase quoted in `source.note` (each such item's `checked.fixed` records the change).

review.how: Check every question, answer and explanation. Fix or delete what is wrong, set status to 'reviewed' with your name and the date, then move the file to packs/ and list it in pack_library.js.

items.question: The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame is in which Ohio city?
items.explain: The Rock Hall sits right on Cleveland's lakefront.

items.question: Cleveland sits on the shore of which Great Lake?
items.explain: The Cuyahoga River flows through Cleveland and into Lake Erie.

items.question: What is Ohio's state bird?
items.explain: The bright red cardinal became Ohio's state bird in 1933.

items.question: Ohio's nickname is the ___ State.
items.explain: Ohio is the Buckeye State, named for its famous tree.

items.question: Ohio's state flower is a red what?
items.explain: The scarlet carnation has been Ohio's state flower since 1904.

items.question: What shape is the Ohio state flag?
items.explain: Ohio has the only state flag that is not a rectangle.

items.question: Ohio's John Glenn was the first American to do what?
items.explain: John Glenn circled the Earth in 1962.

items.question: Ohio's Buckeye candy is chocolate wrapped around what?
items.explain: A peanut butter ball is dipped in chocolate so it looks like a buckeye nut.

items.question: Pierogi, a Cleveland favorite, are dumplings from which country?
items.explain: Pierogi are a Polish favorite, and Cleveland loves them too.

source.note: Fetched 2026-10-07; the page says: 'Dumplings under the name pierogi are a traditional Polish dish'.

checked.fixed: source: common knowledge replaced with en.wikipedia.org (2026-10-07)

items.question: Cedar Point in Ohio is famous for what?
items.explain: Cedar Point is one of the best-known roller coaster parks in the world.

items.question: In Cleveland you can tour the house from which holiday movie?
items.explain: Ralphie's house from A Christmas Story is open to visitors.

items.question: What sport do the Cleveland Cavaliers play?
items.explain: The Cavs have been Cleveland's NBA team since 1970.

items.question: What is the name of Cleveland's pro football team?
items.explain: The Cleveland Browns first took the field in 1946.

items.question: In 2021, Cleveland's baseball team announced it was changing its name from the Indians to what?
items.explain: The team first wore the Guardians name on its uniforms in 2022.

checked.fixed: question: 'In 2022 ... changed its name' is off; the source says the renaming was announced in 2021 (official November 2021) and the name reached uniforms in 2022

items.question: Basketball star LeBron James comes from which Ohio city?
items.explain: LeBron is an Akron native the Cavaliers drafted in 2003.

items.question: Which superhero was created by two Cleveland high school students?
items.explain: Jerry Siegel and Joe Shuster dreamed up Superman in Cleveland.

items.question: Cleveland's West Side Market is a famous what?
items.explain: It is a big indoor market with stalls full of food.

items.question: Ohio is often called the "Mother of" what?
items.explain: Seven U.S. presidents were born in Ohio.

items.question: In which Ohio city did the Wright brothers run their bicycle shop and build their airplane?
items.explain: Their Dayton bicycle shops paid for and powered their flying experiments.

items.question: The Pro Football Hall of Fame is in which Ohio city?
items.explain: Canton got the Hall partly because the NFL was founded there in 1920.

checked.fixed: explanation: source gives three reasons (NFL founded there, Canton Bulldogs, the city's campaign); 'because' -> 'partly because'

items.question: In what year did the Cleveland Cavaliers win their first NBA championship?
items.explain: The 2016 title ended a 52-year wait for a Cleveland championship.

items.question: In the NBA Finals that won the Cavaliers their first championship, they came back from 3 games to 1 down to beat which team?
items.explain: The comeback brought Cleveland its first title in 52 years.

checked.fixed: question: '2016 NBA Finals' gave away the answer to 'what year did the Cavaliers win their first title' in the same pack

items.question: In which year did Cleveland win the World Series by beating the Boston Braves?
items.explain: Cleveland first won a one-game playoff, then beat the Braves in the 1948 Series.

items.question: The Cleveland Browns were named after whom?
answers: The color of the team bus
items.explain: The team took its name from first coach Paul Brown.

items.question: After the original team moved to Baltimore, in what year did the Browns return to Cleveland?
items.explain: The new Browns played their first home game in September 1999.

items.question: In what year did the Cuyahoga River fire make national news?
items.explain: The June 1969 fire made the river a symbol of pollution.

items.question: Cleveland is named after which surveyor who arrived in 1796?
items.explain: The city was first spelled Cleaveland, after Moses Cleaveland.

items.question: A Cleveland "Polish Boy" sandwich is built around which sausage?
items.explain: It is kielbasa on a bun piled with fries, coleslaw and barbecue sauce.

items.question: Thomas Edison was born in 1847 in which small Ohio town?
items.explain: His birthplace in Milan is now a museum.

items.question: Which Ohio-born president later became Chief Justice of the Supreme Court?
items.explain: Taft, from Cincinnati, is the only person to hold both jobs.

items.question: Cedar Point amusement park is in which Ohio city?
items.explain: Cedar Point sits on a Lake Erie peninsula in Sandusky.

items.question: What do the 17 stars on Ohio's flag stand for?
items.explain: Thirteen stars stand for the original states, and four more bring the total to 17, because Ohio was the 17th state.

checked.fixed: explanation: source says 13 of the stars are the original states and the 4 added make 17 for the 17th state; explanation now says so (answer unchanged)

items.question: Cleveland inventor Garrett Morgan created an early version of which everyday device?
items.explain: His 1923 signal added a warning position between stop and go.

items.question: What is Ohio's state motto?
answers: With God, all things are possible
items.correct: With God, all things are possible
items.explain: Ohio adopted this motto in 1959.

items.question: Comedian Bob Hope grew up in Cleveland, but in which country was he born?
items.explain: Bob Hope was born near London and moved to Cleveland in 1908.

items.question: Which Great Lake, Cleveland's lake, is the shallowest of the five?
items.explain: Lake Erie averages only about 62 feet deep.

items.question: In what year did Ohio become a state?
items.explain: Ohio became the 17th state on March 1, 1803.

items.question: How tall is Cleveland's Terminal Tower?
items.explain: Terminal Tower is 708 feet tall to its roof.

checked.fixed: source: ECH Cleveland Union Terminal page gives no height; now Wikipedia: Terminal Tower (roof 708 ft, spire 771 ft); explanation says 'to its roof'

items.question: Which brothers developed Cleveland's Terminal Tower on Public Square?
items.explain: Oris and Mantis Van Sweringen put their railroad terminal on Public Square.

items.question: The West Side Market's landmark building with its clock tower opened in which year?
items.explain: The yellow-brick market house opened in 1912 in Ohio City.

items.question: Which Cleveland architect designed the Ohio state flag?
items.explain: Eisenmann designed it in 1901, and Ohio adopted it in 1902.

items.question: Which Cleveland disc jockey staged the 1952 Moondog Coronation Ball?
items.explain: Alan Freed's early rock shows are a big part of Cleveland's music story.

items.question: From 1903 to 1914, Cleveland's American League team was known by what nickname?
items.explain: Before 1915, when the Indians name arrived, the team was the Naps.

items.question: Before joining the NFL in 1950, the Browns won every title in which league?
items.explain: The Browns won all four AAFC titles from 1946 to 1949.

items.question: Who coached the Browns to the 1964 NFL championship?
items.explain: Blanton Collier led the Browns to the 1964 NFL crown.

items.question: Joseph Bertman's brown mustard, the root of Cleveland's stadium mustards, was first served at which ballpark?
items.explain: Bertman's mustard was first used at League Park in the late 1920s.

items.question: The river name "Cuyahoga" is thought to mean what?
items.explain: The name likely comes from a Native American word for crooked river.

items.question: Ulysses S. Grant was born in which Ohio village?
items.explain: Grant was born in Point Pleasant, Ohio.

items.question: President James A. Garfield was born in a log cabin in what is now which Cuyahoga County village?
items.explain: He was born in Orange Township, which later became Moreland Hills.

items.question: President William McKinley was born in which Ohio town?
items.explain: McKinley was born in Niles and later made his home in Canton.

items.question: Which of the Wright brothers was born in Dayton, Ohio?
items.explain: Orville was born in Dayton in 1871; Wilbur was born in Indiana.

items.question: Which Cedar Point coaster, opened in 2000, was the first full-circuit coaster over 300 feet tall?
items.explain: Millennium Force broke the 300-foot mark in 2000.

items.question: In 1879, Charles Brush lit Cleveland's Public Square with what kind of electric lights?
items.explain: His arc light demonstration made Brush world-famous.

items.question: Jerry Siegel and Joe Shuster met as students at which Cleveland high school?
items.explain: Siegel and Shuster created Superman in 1933 while at Glenville High.

checked.fixed: question: 'Superman's creators' gave away the answer to the superhero question in the same pack

items.question: Neil Armstrong was born in 1930 in which Ohio town?
items.explain: Wapakoneta is the hometown of the first man on the Moon.
